title: Kiss (band)
wiki_lead:
Kiss (commonly styled in all caps as KISS) was an American rock band formed in New York City in 1973 by Paul Stanley (vocals, rhythm guitar), Gene Simmons (vocals, bass guitar), Ace Frehley (lead guitar, vocals) and Peter Criss (drums, vocals). Known for their face paint and stage outfits, the group rose to prominence in the mid-1970s with shock rock–style live performances that featured fire-breathing, blood-spitting, smoking guitars, shooting rockets, levitating drum kits and pyrotechnics. The band went through several lineup changes, starting with drummer Eric Carr replacing original drummer Peter Criss in 1980, with Stanley and Simmons remaining the only consistent members. The final lineup consisted of Stanley, Simmons, Tommy Thayer (lead guitar, vocals) and Eric Singer (drums, vocals).
With their makeup and costumes, the band members took on the personas of comic book-style characters: the Starchild (Stanley), the Demon (Simmons), the Spaceman or Space Ace (Frehley), and the Catman (Criss). During the second half of the 1970s, Kiss became one of America's most successful rock bands and a pop culture phenomenon. The band's commercial success declined during the early 1980s; however, it experienced a resurgence in 1983 when the band members began performing without makeup and costumes, marking the beginning of the band's "unmasked" era that would last until 1996. The first album of this era, 1983's platinum-certified Lick It Up, successfully introduced the band to a new generation of fans, and its music videos received regular airplay on MTV. In response to a wave of Kiss nostalgia in the mid-1990s, the original lineup reunited in 1996; at this time, the band resumed using makeup and stage costumes. The resulting 1996–1997 reunion tour was the band's most successful, grossing $143.7 million. In January 2019, Kiss began its final worldwide tour, and the band retired after performing its final show in New York City in December 2023. They have since reunited occasionally to attend Kiss-related events and record new music.
Kiss is regarded as one of the most influential rock bands of all time, as well as one of the best selling bands of all time. Kiss has also earned 30 Gold albums, the most of any band from the United States. Kiss has earned 14 Platinum albums, three of which earned multi-Platinum status. The four original members of Kiss (Simmons, Stanley, Criss, and Frehley) were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in April 2014. Kiss was ranked by MTV as the ninth-greatest metal band of all time, placed tenth on VH1's "100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock" list, was ranked as the third "Best Metal and Hard Rock Live Band of All Time" by Loudwire magazine, and was placed sixteenth by the British magazine Classic Rock on their "The 50 Best Rock Bands of All Time" list.

grok_lead: Kiss is an American hard rock band formed in New York City in 1973 by vocalist and rhythm guitarist Paul Stanley, bassist and vocalist Gene Simmons, lead guitarist and vocalist Ace Frehley, and drummer and vocalist Peter Criss. The group rose to prominence in the mid-1970s with their signature kabuki-inspired face paint, elaborate costumes, and larger-than-life stage personas âStanley as the Starchild, Simmons as the Demon, Frehley as the Spaceman, and Criss as the Catmanâpaired with high-energy live shows featuring pyrotechnics, smoke bombs, and guitar solos shot from the air. Known for anthemic hard rock anthems like " Rock and Roll All Nite " and "Shout It Out Loud," Kiss became one of the best-selling bands of all time, with certified sales exceeding 30 gold albums (the most for any American group) and 14 platinum albums, including multi-platinum certifications for releases such as Destroyer (1976) and Double Platinum (1978). Over their five-decade career, Kiss evolved from their 1970s glam rock roots into a multimedia empire, releasing over 20 studio albums, launching merchandise lines, starring in films like Kiss Meets the Phantom of the Park (1978), and even launching a comic book series that debuted with the largest single-day sales in the history of the medium at the time. The band's lineup underwent several changes, with Frehley and Criss departing in the early 1980s amid internal tensions and substance abuse issues, leading to the addition of guitarists Vinnie Vincent, Mark St. John, and Bruce Kulick, and drummers Eric Carr (who died in 1991) and Eric Singer; later, Tommy Thayer replaced Frehley on lead guitar in 2002. A highly publicized reunion of the original four members in 1996 produced the album Psycho Circus and a massively successful world tour, but tensions resurfaced, resulting in another split by 2002. Kiss's influence extends beyond music, pioneering the rock spectacle and fan club culture through the KISS Army, while achieving milestones like induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014 and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1999. The band concluded touring with their End of the Road farewell tour's final show on December 2, 2023, at Madison Square Garden, marking the close of over 2,000 live performances. In 2025, Kiss received the Kennedy Center Honors, recognizing the band's original lineup, with Ace Frehley honored posthumously. Tragically, founding member Ace Frehley passed away on October 16, 2025, at age 74, following a fall that led to a brain bleed, shortly after canceling tour dates due to health issues. Despite retirement from the road, Kiss performed at the KISS Kruise event in Las Vegas on November 14â16, 2025, marking their first unmasked appearance since retirement and including a tribute to Ace Frehley.
